inputs.share_count_basis: 626.99m shares outstanding on the Q3-2026 10-Q cover (21 Oct 2026) plus ~2m treasury-method dilution from options/RSUs; held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. Buybacks are running far ahead of SBC (TTM $2.99bn vs $76m SBC) and are debt/asset-sale funded, so the falling count is a capital-structure choice, not modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30 Sep 2026 = FY2025 $71m + 9M-2026 $57m - 9M-2025 $52m (10-Q Q3-2026 segment note, footnote 2; 10-K FY2025 cash flow). No combined reconciliation figure is published, so the $7m of 9M-2026 tax withholding on vesting (financing activities) is added on top.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build (patacas/HKD are USD-pegged; SGD exposure partly hedged). Risk-free ~4.3%, ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~1.15 -> cost of equity ~10%. Pre-tax cost of debt 4.7% (10-Q weighted average) with almost no tax shield (interest sits in zero/low-tax Macao and a US parent with no taxable income). Weights ~65% equity+NCI / 35% debt at market -> ~8.3%, rounded up to 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: two-jurisdiction, China-consumer and concession-renewal risk is charged in the flows, the terminal cap and the scenario weights, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: $147m of finance leases are inside total_debt; operating leases are immaterial. Leasehold interests in land (Macao land concessions, Singapore land premium) are amortised inside the D&A path and their cash cost sits in the capex path (the MBS expansion land premium was paid 2019/April 2025/March 2026 and is behind us).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; the 24.44% Sands China minority is deducted ONCE, in the equity bridge, at a model-consistent value rather than attributable-only flows. Macao TTM adjusted property EBITDA ~$2.20bn x ~9x (the multiple the base case implies for the group) less ~$5.2bn SCL net debt = ~$14.6bn SCL equity x 24.44% = ~$3.5bn. The market marks the same stake at ~$2.7bn (1928.HK HK$10.67 x ~8.09bn shares / 7.8455 x 24.44%, 13 Nov 2026); the higher figure is used so the minority is not under-deducted against an EV that values Macao above market.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, cyclical, non-US operations -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). LVS is an integrated-resort operator, not a REIT or holdco: value is the unlevered cash flow of two concession-based resort franchises. FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30 Sep 2026 so the flows start where the balance sheet ends; Y1 = Oct-2026 to Sep-2027. reported_fcf $2,406m = TTM OCF $3,487m - capex $1,081m and is LEVERED (after ~$675m cash interest) and pre-NCI; last_fcf strips SBC + equity taxes. The component build is unlevered: TTM pre-SBC EBITDA $4,594m (33.8%) = adjusted property EBITDA $5,073m - corporate ex-SBC $281m - pre-opening $18m - development $180m. Interest income not stripped: the company is in net debt, and the build starts from EBITDA so interest never enters. Buyback status: active repurchaser ($2.99bn TTM, $5.06bn authorisation remaining to July 2029) funding well beyond owner FCF with the $1.26bn seller-note repayment and debt; shareholders' equity is now negative (-$344m). Restricted cash $125m ignored. Price is a regular-session close, not after-hours. Horizon 10 years because the MBS expansion capex (FY2027-30) and its earnings (from Jan 2031) must both be inside the explicit period before capitalising.

equity_bridge.note: Model-consistent value of the SCL minority; see inputs.nci_treatment. 10-Q Q3-2026: LVS ownership of SCL 75.56% at 30 Sep 2026.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: normalised Macao GGR growth (~2-3%, sell-side cut through 2026) plus Marina Bay Sands volume/ADR growth; no historical CAGR is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-19%/-11%) diverges from revenue CAGR (+47%/+35%) by far more than 30pp and neither is a usable growth anchor: revenue CAGRs are measured off COVID-closure bases (FY2020 $2.9bn, FY2022 $4.1bn) and equity is shrinking because buybacks exceed earnings (stockholders' equity -$344m at Q3-2026). The honest long-run comparison is FY2019 Asia-only revenue $12.1bn -> FY2025 $13.0bn, ~1.2%/yr.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC, levered): FY2023 $2,138m, FY2024 $1,559m, FY2025 $1,784m, TTM $2,323m; FY2022 OCF is not in the XBRL extract so no 3-year figure. FY2025 OCF absorbed an $848m Singapore land-premium payment booked in operating activities. SBC is ~0.6% of revenue, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are effectively the same. FY2022 EPS includes the gain on the Las Vegas sale; FY2020 EPS was negative, so the 5-year EPS CAGR is undefined.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA after corporate, pre-opening and development expense. TTM 33.8% (two low-hold quarters); FY2025 35.9% (MBS hold 23.4%, above normal). Path normalises hold and lets development expense (digital gaming wind-down, $180m TTM) roll off, offset by Macao promotional intensity and Singapore's tiered casino tax.
base.capex_note: TTM capex 7.9% of revenue. Remaining MBS expansion ~$4.9bn of the $8.0bn budget (incl. ~$0.5bn financing cost that is not capex here) spread ~$1.0/1.25/1.25/0.9bn over Y1-Y4 on top of ~$0.95bn/yr maintenance plus Macao Investment Plan spend; 8% thereafter for perpetual resort reinvestment and whatever a post-2032 Macao concession demands.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: TTM tax expense $400m on model EBIT ~$3.0bn = 13.2%; cash taxes are almost entirely Singapore (17%). Macao gaming profit is exempt through 2027 with a dividend-tax substitute. Ramps to 16% as Singapore's share grows and the Macao arrangement is renewed on somewhat worse terms.
base.terminal_note: 13x terminal FCF cap (cyclical, concession-based franchise; Macao concession expires Dec 2032 and renewal is assumed, not owned).

scenario_narratives.base: Macao gross gaming revenue grows 2-3% a year and Sands holds the mass-market share it has rebuilt (26% in Q3-2026), but the promotional environment among the six concessionaires stays competitive, so Macao property margins do not recover to FY2023-24 levels. Marina Bay Sands table hold reverts to normal after two soft quarters, volumes and room rates keep growing mid-single digit, and Singapore's tiered casino tax takes a slightly larger share. Digital-gaming development spend rolls off. The $8.0bn MBS expansion is built on budget through 2030 and opens in January 2031, adding roughly $1bn of revenue over two years at group-like margins, a high-single-digit cash return rather than the returns management targets. Both concessions are renewed (Macao at end-2032) on terms that cost a little more tax and a standing reinvestment burden.
scenario_narratives.bull: China consumer confidence and outbound travel recover, Macao GGR compounds mid-single digit and the Londoner Grand and premium-mass strategy push Sands' share and Macao margins back toward pre-2025 levels as promotional spending rationalises. Marina Bay Sands keeps its lead over Resorts World Sentosa through the RWS 2.0 rebuild, and the expansion (new tower, arena, premium gaming) opens on time into a supply-constrained duopoly and earns mid-teens returns. Group EBITDA margin reaches 38% and the Macao concession and tax arrangements are renewed on unchanged terms.
scenario_narratives.bear: A China slowdown or a PRC policy shift on capital flows and outbound gambling leaves Macao GGR flat for years while the six concessionaires keep buying share with reinvestment, compressing Macao margins further. Marina Bay Sands loses premium-mass share to a rebuilt Resorts World Sentosa from 2030, the expansion runs over budget and ramps slowly into a more competitive Singapore, and higher tax tiers bite. Macao's profits-tax exemption lapses after 2027 and the 2032 concession is renewed only with a heavier tax and investment burden. This case does not price outright non-renewal of the Macao concession, which would be worse than the bear value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: every dollar of cash flow depends on two regulators, the Macao concession expires inside the forecast horizon (Dec 2032), leverage is rising while buybacks outrun free cash flow, and Macao margins are already eroding. Base 50%: slow Macao growth with normal hold and an on-budget expansion is what current evidence supports. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs a China consumer recovery, a truce in Macao promotions and a high-return MBS expansion, three largely independent things, to all go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: LVS is valued as two concession-based resort franchises on unlevered owner free cash flow, with the Sands China minority and $12.6bn of net debt deducted once each. The next four years carry roughly $4.4bn of Marina Bay Sands expansion capex that depresses free cash flow before the earnings arrive in 2031, so a ten-year horizon is used and the terminal value is capped at a cyclical-franchise multiple rather than left to Gordon growth. SBC is immaterial (~0.6% of revenue), so the house and street values nearly coincide. The stock's real swing factors are leverage on the equity (every 1x of EV/EBITDA is roughly $7 a share) and whether the concessions renew on current terms.
key_risks_to_valuation: Macao concession expires 31 Dec 2032; terminal value assumes renewal. Non-renewal would remove roughly 45% of EBITDA and is not priced in any scenario.
Financial leverage: net debt plus the SCL minority is ~$16bn against ~$25bn of equity value, so small changes in margin or the terminal multiple move the per-share value disproportionately.
MBS expansion returns: ~$8.0bn of spend is assumed to earn a high-single-digit cash return in the base case; management targets materially more, a slow ramp against RWS 2.0 would deliver less.
Hold volatility: FY2025 margins were flattered by above-normal MBS hold and the TTM is depressed by below-normal hold; the normalised margin (34-35%) is a judgment between the two.
Macao profits-tax exemption and the dividend-tax substitution agreement both end 31 Dec 2027 pending extension.
Buybacks ($3.0bn TTM) exceed owner FCF and are partly debt-funded; the model holds net debt at the 30 Sep 2026 level and does not credit accretion or charge the added leverage.
NCI is deducted at a fixed ~$3.5bn in every scenario; it would be lower in the bear case and higher in the bull.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 35.03-70.45. Sands China (1928.HK) and USDHKD from the same API for the NCI cross-check.
data_sources.financials: LVS 10-Q Q3-2026 (balance sheet, debt note, cash flow, segment and EBITDA reconciliation, cover share count), 10-K FY2025 (EBITDA reconciliation, taxes paid), LVS_Metrics.csv and the kpis table (adjusted property EBITDA by property).
data_sources.qualitative: LVS_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): Macao competition and GGR forecasts, MBS expansion budget and timeline, Macao Investment Plan, concession and tax-arrangement expiries, capital-return programme.
